title: How Much Money Do You Need to Start Investing?
summary: How much money do you need to start investing? Often only a few dollars. See how fractional shares, fund minimums, fees and a cash buffer set your real starting amount.
body_markdown:
## Sources and further reading


Checked July 16, 2026. Community posts and videos are included as perspectives; official sources carry the factual authority.


1. [Investing in Fractional Shares](https://www.finra.org/investors/insights/investing-fractional-shares)


FINRA · regulator


Access benefits plus transfer, execution, hours, and voting limitations.


2. [Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs)](https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/investing-basics/investment-products/mutual-funds-and-exchange-traded-2)


Investor.gov · government


ETF shares trade on exchanges at market prices that may differ from NAV.


3. [Mutual Funds](https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/investing-basics/investment-products/mutual-funds-and-exchange-traded-1)


Investor.gov · government


Funds set their own initial and subsequent purchase amounts; purchases happen at the next calculated NAV plus fees; read the prospectus.


4. [Index Funds](https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/investing-basics/investment-products/mutual-funds-and-exchange-traded-4)


Investor.gov · government


How index funds work, costs, tracking error, concentration risk, and due diligence.


5. [Introduction to Investing](https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing)


Investor.gov · government


Goals, time horizon, regular investing, diversification, emergency savings, and high-interest debt.


6. [Compound Interest Calculator](https://www.investor.gov/financial-tools-calculators/calculators/compound-interest-calculator)


Investor.gov · government


A scenario tool for exploring contributions, time, and assumed rates without presenting a forecast as fact.


7. [How Fees and Expenses Affect Your Investment Portfolio](https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/general-resources/news-alerts/alerts-bulletins/investor-bulletins/updated)


Investor.gov · government


The compounding effect of ongoing fees and where to find fee disclosures.
